newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL STOCKS END LOWER AS WALL STREET SLUMPS.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL STOCKS END LOWER AS WALL STREET SLUMPS.

text.p: Brazilian shares closed down 1.59 percent on Thursday amid a wave of profit-taking, weighed down by declines in U.S. stocks and speculation ahead of futures and options expiries, brokers said.
"The market rose a lot yesterday, so we had some profit-taking today," a dealer at local Schahin Cury brokerage said.
The Sao Paulo bolsa's Bovespa index .BVSP of 47 most-traded shares dropped 201 points to end at 12,322 points on volume of 800.96 million reais ($738.2 million).

Brokers said losses on Wall Street and jostling ahead of August 13 futures settlements and August 18 options expiration prompted many investors to book profits after Wednesday's sharp 5.19 percent rise in the Bovespa.
"The market will remain volatile until the settlements are over," said a broker at local Misasi brokerage.
Especially hard hit in the session was benchmark Telebras, which regularly accounts for 65 percent of daily trade.
Telebras' benchmark preferred, which had soared seven percent on Wednesday, retreated 2.24 percent to end at 153 reais.
